correctness.rationale: For every finite positive integer m, F_m(s)=(1-s)(s+s^{-1})^{m-1}-s^2 has one root in (0,1) by strict monotonicity. The explicitly defined positive continuous h satisfies Mh=lambda h at each finite branch, at the interface n=m, and at infinity. Since 1<=h<=c, exact spectral radius r(M)=lambda>2 follows from positive-order bounds. M=S+K with ||S||<=2 and K finite rank, hence T=M/lambda is quasi-compact. All seeds contain 0 uniformly by m+1 steps and an arbitrary isolated k after m+1+k steps, giving primitivity. The published compact-substitution theorem yields strict ergodicity. The expansion lambda-2=4^{1-m}(1+O(2^{-m})) follows from the defining root equation. The exact binomial partial-sum inequality and rational root bound prove the m=7 72000-step reversal. Standalone finite checker from this very package passes 1101 checks, but the universal result is established analytically.
